slot.brief: Solve dy/dx + P(x)y = Q(x) with a non-obvious P(x) (e.g. involving 1/x or trig) using integrating factor; find particular solution given y(0).

verdicts.working: The integrating factor is \(\sec x\), so \((y\sec x)'=\tan x\). Integrating gives \(y=\cos x(C-\ln(\cos x))\). From \(y(0)=1\), \(C=1\), matching (A).

Independent check: The integrating factor is \(\sec x\), so \((y\sec x)'=\tan x\). Integrating gives \(y=\cos x(C-\ln(\cos x))\). From \(y(0)=1\), \(C=1\), matching (A).
solution:
The integrating factor is $e^{\int \tan x\,dx}=\sec x$, so $\frac{d}{dx}(y\sec x)=\tan x$.
$$y\sec x=-\ln(\cos x)+C$$
Using $y(0)=1$ gives $C=1$, hence $y=\cos x\left(1-\ln(\cos x)\right)$.
